tasks.analysis: The earliest ancestor of the modern bicycle is probably a machine used in England in the early 1800s called a hobbyhorse. It had two wheels and a place to sit but no pedals; riders would push it along with their feet. Later, an inventor added pedals directly to the front wheel, like a modern child’s tricycle. This version, with a huge front wheel, was faster, but it was unsafe.
